svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Component · Blended clip row · not-available · wide
svg.desc: Mirrors App/BlendedClipRow.swift for a clip whose file is neither on this device nor on PicPlace (2026-09-26, plan §15 — "A clip that is not here claims only what PicPlace holds" — and §16): PicPlace's list for the project has been read and does not name the file, or PicPlace holds none of the project's heavy files (PicPlaceController.blendAvailability == .notOnPicPlace). It happens to a blend that was only ever on the device that made it — Victory Bridge Sunset on the 18 Pro, whose six rows used to say On PicPlace and offer a Download that failed four times. The row keeps the blend's still (posters/<blend id>.jpg rides the records bundle even when the clip never went up) with components/holdings-pill.blend.nowhere.svg at 0.8, 2 pt in — the slashed layers alone (square.3.layers.3d.slash), no cloud: PicPlace holds none of it. The subtitle leads with "Not available to download · " (BlendWhereLine), and there is no button: BlendDownloadButton draws nothing unless the list holds the file, so the text column runs to the row's Spacer (x 335 — HStack spacing 12 before it, 14 padding). While the list is still unread (.unknown) the row claims neither way: the plain subtitle, no button, and holdings-pill.blend.there (grey layers, no cloud). A tap on the row still asks (the parent's onPlay → .fetchPrompt), and the prompt can only say the clip isn't on PicPlace (FetchOffer.notUploaded / .unavailable). The words are interim — Steven's copy pass (docs/TODO.md). 2026-11-06 (docs/approved-assets.md): every row ends in the approve seal — ApproveToggle (App/ApprovedAssetViews.swift), a 28 pt hit area in the row's HStack(spacing: 12) between the text column and the trailing button: checkmark.seal 17 pt medium in secondary 70 % until the output is approved, checkmark.seal.fill in LL.accent after (the approved and edited.approved states); a press toggles. Here, with no trailing button, it ends at the row's 14 pt inset (centred 28 pt in). The text column ends 12 pt before it (223 pt from x 84), so the same real strings clip sooner.

g.text: Not available to download · 24 fps · yesterday
